topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the administrative opening, course context, and learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Processes, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the broad causes of cancer by examining the interplay between intrinsic cellular errors, genetic predisposition, and environmental risk factors identified through epidemiological observations.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenic Agents and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the specific molecular and cellular mechanisms by which biological, chemical, and physical agents induce DNA damage or promote neoplastic growth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine whether environmental agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This topic delivers the concluding summary on environmental cancer risks and personal risk-benefit decisions to close the lecture.
